column4: The ayah says Moses was called by his Lord in the sacred valley of Tuwa; it is another direct formulation of Tûr as the place of divine address.

Humans and jinn are addressed together but cannot pass beyond the regions of heaven and earth without authority; this concretely joins the section's human/jinn distinction to its boundary-crossing sense.
The jinn do not know Solomon has died until his body falls; this gives a specific contrast to the section's account of ins as manifest and jinn as hidden.
The wild creatures are gathered on the Day of Resurrection; this matches the section's secondary ṭ-w-r sense for wild animals beyond the settled human boundary.
God makes people's own houses places of repose and animal skins into dwellings; this concretizes the section's account of a settled place formed by its residents.
Shelters are made even from mountains, along with protective clothing; this makes the mountain a human refuge beyond the section's town-versus-wilderness boundary.
Fighting is prohibited at the Sacred Mosque unless the other side fights there; this specifies a protected boundary around the sanctuary in the section's secure-town image.
Expelling people from the Sacred Mosque is named among the grave offenses; this gives the sanctuary's people a specific claim to remain within its protected boundary.
The verse says not to transgress God's limits; this echoes the section's dictionary idiom for going beyond one's own boundary, while shifting from a dwelling boundary to a legal one.
Troublemakers in Madinah are threatened with removal so they will no longer live there except briefly; this makes residence in the bounded city conditional on its social order.

The spider's house is called the weakest of houses, reversing the section's dictionary association of a person's home with safety; the verse's main subject is false reliance, so the bridge is limited.
The elephant-people story introduces a threat to the sanctuary's security; 105 itself does not name the House, while the following Quraysh surah names the House and safety.
The elephant force's plan is made to fail; this is the event's own contribution to the sanctuary-protection theme, completed by 106:3-4, though 105 does not name Mecca.
Flocks of birds are sent against the elephant force; this specifies how the assault is halted, while 106:3-4 names the House and its safety.
The birds pelt the force with stones of baked clay; this supplies the means of protection in the episode preceding Quraysh's security passage.
The attackers are left like eaten straw; this completes the failed assault whose sanctuary setting is made explicit in 106:3-4, although 105 itself leaves the House unnamed.
